title: Chapter 49: The Beguiling Boy 4
content:
Chapter 49

The Beguiling Boy 4

Wei Wuxian finally realized which moment in history he had stumbled into.

Years ago, acting on battlefield intelligence, Nie Mingjue had led a surprise raid on Yangquan.

Chifeng-zun’s preemptive strikes were notoriously devastating, carving through enemy lines without fail. Yet whether due to an intelligence leak or simply a terrible twist of fate, no one could have anticipated the disaster awaiting them: the raid ran headfirst into the patriarch of the Qishan Wen Clan himself—Wen Ruohan.

Dramatically underestimating the enemy's strength, the tables were turned on them. The Qishan Wen Sect wiped out the strike force and dragged the captured survivors back to Nightless City as chained prisoners.

Meng Yao dropped to one knee beside Nie Mingjue, murmuring, "I truly never imagined I would see the day where you, Sect Leader, were reduced to such a pathetic state."

Nie Mingjue spat out two venomous words: "Piss off."

A faint, pitying laugh drifted from Meng Yao's lips. "Still think you’re the King of Hejian? Open your eyes and take a look around. You're in the Sun Palace now."

A captured cultivator pinned nearby spat into the dirt, sneering, "Sun Palace? Nothing more than a kennel for Wen dogs!"

Meng Yao’s expression iced over. In a flash of cold steel, his sword cleared its scabbard.

A crimson line erupted across the man’s throat; before he could even choke out a groan, he crumpled to the stone floor. His clan brothers wailed in horror, lunging forward with desperate cries. Nie Mingjue’s eyes flared with pure fury: "You—!"

Another cultivator roared through gritted teeth, "Wen dog! If you have the guts, kill me too—"

Meng Yao didn’t even twitch a brow. With a backhanded sweep of his blade, he opened the man's throat in a geyser of blood, smiling pleasantly. "Gladly."

Standing tall before the expanding pool of gore, two white-robed corpses sprawled at his boots, he offered a polite, charming grin. "Anyone else care to use that word?"

Nie Mingjue’s voice dropped low and lethal: "Wen dog."

Knowing full well that falling into Wen Ruohan’s clutches was a death sentence, he harbored zero fear. Had Wei Wuxian been in his shoes, he would have done the exact same thing: curse them out to his heart's content, since he was doomed anyway.

Meng Yao merely chuckled, entirely unbothered. He snapped his fingers. A Wen cultivator shuffled forward on his knees, lifting a long wooden lacquered box high above his crown with trembling hands. Meng Yao flipped the latch, drawing out the weapon resting inside. "Sect Leader Nie, care to see what this is?"

It was Nie Mingjue’s personal saber—Baxia!

Nie Mingjue roared, "Get your hands off it!"

Meng Yao held Baxia up, letting the blade catch the torchlight as he turned it in his grip. "Sect Leader Nie, Baxia passed through my hands plenty of times in the past. Aren't you a little late to be throwing a tantrum?"

Nie Mingjue ground out every syllable through clenched teeth: "Take. Your filthy hands. Off."

As if deliberately poking a wounded beast, Meng Yao weighed the heavy saber in his palm, casually critiquing the steel. "This saber of yours... I suppose it barely passes as a first-rate spiritual weapon. Still, it falls a bit short compared to the blade wielded by your late father, the old Sect Leader Nie. Why don't you take a guess: how many slaps will it take for Sect Leader Wen to snap this one in half?"

Every drop of blood in Nie Mingjue’s veins rushed straight to his head. Caught in the slipstream of his incandescent wrath, Wei Wuxian’s borrowed scalp tingled with sheer numbness.

Vicious, Wei Wuxian thought grimly. Deadly vicious.

If there was one thing in this world Nie Mingjue loathed above all else—the one wound that would never heal—it was the death of his father.

Years ago, when Nie Mingjue was barely a teenager and his father still reigned over the Qinghe Nie Clan, a rare, masterwork saber had been offered as tribute to Wen Ruohan. Delighted with the prize, Wen Ruohan spent days admiring it, casually asking his gathered guest retainers what they thought of the blade.

Wen Ruohan was notoriously volatile—smiling one second, skinning someone alive the next. Naturally, the sycophants scrambled to shower him with lavish praise, hailing the weapon as an peerless marvel without equal. But whether out of a petty grudge against Old Sect Leader Nie or simply desperate to stand out from the fawning crowd, one guest retainer spoke up: Your Excellency's saber is naturally beyond compare. However, I fear there is someone who might beg to differ.

Wen Ruohan’s mood soured instantly, demanding to know who. The retainer sneered that it was none other than the Sect Leader of Qinghe Nie. He pointed out that the Nie Clan was renowned across the realm for their saber path, and Old Sect Leader Nie constantly bragged that his family's blades were invincible and unmatched under the heavens, claiming no weapon forged in centuries could hold a candle to his own. He warned Wen Ruohan that no matter how exquisite this tribute was, Old Sect Leader Nie would never acknowledge it—and even if he paid lip service, his heart would secretly spit on it.

Hearing this, Wen Ruohan burst into booming laughter, amused by the defiance. He summoned Old Sect Leader Nie to Qishan on the spot, demanded his personal saber, and examined it from his high seat. Handing it back, he offered a single remark: “Mm, a fine blade indeed.” He casually patted the steel a few times, then dismissed him.

Nothing seemed out of the ordinary at the time. Old Sect Leader Nie hadn't thought much of the bizarre summons, merely irritated by being jerked around like a common servant. But a few days after returning home, during a routine night-hunt, his saber cleaved into a savage beast—only to abruptly shatter into several pieces. Caught completely defenseless, he took the full force of the charging beast's horn through his chest, maimed beyond repair.

Nie Mingjue, who had ridden beside his father on that hunt, watched the entire nightmare unfold with his own eyes.

Though dragged back alive, Old Sect Leader Nie couldn't swallow the burning humiliation, nor could his shattered spiritual veins mend. After lingering in bed for six agonizing months, he finally breathed his last. No one could say for sure whether he had died from his wounds or simply choked to death on sheer, impotent rage. That was the bloody root of Qinghe Nie’s bone-deep hatred for the Qishan Wen Clan.

And now, right in front of Wen Ruohan himself, Meng Yao was holding Baxia, gleefully picking at the scab of his father's ruined saber and gruesome death. It was pure, unadulterated poison.

Nie Mingjue lashed out with a brutal palm strike, sending Meng Yao stumbling backward with a spray of fresh blood. Seeing the scuffle, the shadowy silhouette on the jade throne leaned forward, about to intervene. Meng Yao scrambled to his feet in a flash, lunging forward to plant a vicious kick squarely into Nie Mingjue’s chest. Having poured every ounce of his remaining strength into that desperate palm strike, Nie Mingjue crashed heavily onto the floor, the mouthful of hot blood he’d been choking down finally erupting across the stone.

Wei Wuxian’s jaw dropped in absolute shock.

Of all the wild rumors and bar gossip he'd heard about the Sunshot Campaign, he had never imagined that the grand saga included Lianfang-zun stomping Chifeng-zun into the dirt!

Meng Yao pinned Nie Mingjue down with a heavy boot to his ribs, barking, "How dare you act wildly before Sect Leader Wen!"

He drove his sword downward in a lethal thrust. Nie Mingjue slammed a palm upward against the flat of the steel, the concussive force shattering Meng Yao's blade into jagged metal shards. Meng Yao was thrown back by the blast. Just as Nie Mingjue’s second palm strike was descending toward his skull, a bizarre, violent suction ripped him sideways across the hall.

The pull was dragging him straight toward Wen Ruohan’s jade throne. Nie Mingjue skidded across the black stone, leaving a smeared trail of gore stretching thirty feet long.

Snapping a hand out, Nie Mingjue seized a kneeling Wen disciple and hurled him like a projectile toward the throne. With a sickening wet burst, the disciple detonated midair like an overripe melon smashed with an iron sledgehammer, brain matter and blood painting the floor. Wen Ruohan had pulverized the man's skull with a single careless flick of spiritual energy.

Yet the distraction bought Nie Mingjue the heartbeat he needed. Bolstered by volcanic rage, a surge of adrenaline gave him monstrous strength; leaping to his feet, his fingers snapped through an invocation seal, summoning Baxia whistling through the air into his grip.

Meng Yao shouted, "Sect Leader, watch out!"

A voice echoed from the dais in wild, arrogant laughter: "Let him come!"

It sounded like a young man's voice. Wei Wuxian wasn't surprised; Wen Ruohan’s cultivation had long transcended mortal limits, naturally keeping his physical prime preserved at its absolute peak.

The instant Nie Mingjue’s fingers closed around Baxia’s hilt, he unleashed a sweeping cleave, instantly slicing the dozen Wen cultivators swarming him in two at the waist!

Broken corpses collapsed across the polished obsidian stone. Suddenly, an icy shiver rocketed up Wei Wuxian’s spine.

A phantom silhouette had materialized directly behind them. Nie Mingjue whipped around with a savage horizontal slash, his spiritual energy pulverizing a wide trench through the masonry. But the strike met only empty air. Before he could recover his guard, a concussive shockwave caved into his chest, launching him headfirst into a gilded pillar. He coughed up another mouthful of hot blood, fresh gore trickling down his brow to blur his vision. Sensing an approaching presence, he swung his saber blindly—only for a thunderous fist to drive straight into his sternum, embedding his broad frame inches into the solid stone floor!

Sharing his physical senses, Wei Wuxian felt his borrowed skull throbbing with blinding agony, thoroughly chilled by the brutality.

Wen Ruohan’s strength was genuinely terrifying—an overwhelming, suffocating nightmare.

Wei Wuxian had never traded blows with Nie Mingjue in his prime, so he couldn't say who would win in a duel, but from what he had observed, Nie Mingjue easily ranked among the top three cultivators alive. Yet even with that monstrous foundation, he was rendered utterly helpless before Wen Ruohan! Wei Wuxian honestly doubted that if he were standing there in his own flesh, he would have fared any better...

Wen Ruohan planted a heavy boot on Nie Mingjue’s chest. Wei Wuxian’s vision swam with encroaching darkness, the iron tang of blood welling up in his throat.

Meng Yao’s footsteps approached at a measured pace. "Your subordinate is incompetent, forcing Sect Leader to dirty his own hands."

Wen Ruohan chuckled coldly. "Useless trash."

Meng Yao mirrored the smile without a hint of offense.

Wen Ruohan asked, "He was the one who killed Wen Xu?"

"Indeed. It was him," Meng Yao replied smoothly. "Sect Leader, do you wish to execute the murderer here and now, or haul him down to the Earthfire Hall? Personally, I suggest the Earthfire Hall would be far more fitting."

The "Earthfire Hall" was Wen Ruohan’s private dungeon—a personal slaughterhouse packed with thousands of bespoke torture devices designed for prolonged, agonizing torment. Meng Yao clearly had no intention of granting Nie Mingjue a quick death; he wanted to drag him to Wen Ruohan's abattoir, using the very torture implements he had designed to slowly butcher him alive.

Listening to the two of them casually laughing over how to carve him up, raw fury scorched Nie Mingjue’s insides, blood boiling behind his teeth.

Wen Ruohan grunted, "What's the point of dragging half-dead meat around?"

Meng Yao countered with easy flattery, "You can't say that, Sect Leader. With Sect Leader Nie's formidable constitution, a couple days of recuperation might just have him roaring with vitality again."

Wen Ruohan waved a dismissive hand. "Handle it as you see fit."

"Understood."

Yet right as the word left his lips, an impossibly thin streak of silver light sliced through the air.

Wen Ruohan’s breath was cut off without a sound.

A spray of warm, fresh blood spattered across Nie Mingjue’s face. Sensing the sudden shift, he strained with everything he had to pry his eyes open and see what had happened. But his battered body gave out; his head dropped heavily to the stone, his eyes falling shut.

Wei Wuxian had no idea how much time drifted by before the dark blur faded, Nie Mingjue’s heavy eyelids fluttering open.

The moment consciousness returned, he found himself slung over Meng Yao’s shoulder, being half-dragged, half-carried down a dark mountain path.

Meng Yao rasped, "Sect Leader Nie?"

Nie Mingjue growled, "Is Wen Ruohan dead?"

Meng Yao’s footing stumbled slightly, his voice shaking with residual adrenaline. "He should be... yes. He's dead."

He was still clutching something in his free hand.

Nie Mingjue’s voice dropped to a dark rumble: "Give me the saber."

Wei Wuxian couldn't see Meng Yao’s face, but the bitter, self-deprecating chuckle in his voice was unmistakable. "Sect Leader Nie... at a time like this, must you really keep thinking about cutting my head off...?"

Nie Mingjue held his breath, gathered his scattered spiritual strength, and snatched the weapon back with a lightning-fast swipe. Quick as Meng Yao was, pure raw strength trumped speed; unable to keep his grip, the youth sprang backward to put distance between them. "Sect Leader Nie, you are severely injured!"

Heavy steel back in his grip, Nie Mingjue’s tone was pure ice: "You murdered them."

Those captive cultivators dragged to Nightless City alongside him.

Meng Yao pleaded, "Sect Leader Nie, you saw the situation back there... I had no other choice."

Nie Mingjue despised cowardly excuses above all else. Fury flared in his chest; slashing Baxia through the air, he roared, "No choice?! Doing it was your choice! Killing them was your choice!"

Dodging the razor-sharp wind, Meng Yao scrambled to defend himself. "Was it really up to me?! Sect Leader Nie, if you and I were to trade places—"

Knowing exactly what manipulative garbage was coming, Nie Mingjue barked, "I would never!"

Exhaustion finally catching up to him, Meng Yao stumbled over loose gravel as he desperately weaved away from the relentless swings, his pristine composure cracking into ragged panic. He wheezed for air, then suddenly snapped, screaming at the top of his lungs:

"Chifeng-zun! Do you honestly not understand?! If I hadn't killed them, the corpse rotting on that floor would be you!!!"

Strip away the drama, and the sentence was essentially: I saved your miserable life, you owe me, and butchering me makes you an ungrateful hypocrite. But Meng Yao was a master of rhetoric; wrapping the truth in wounded grief and righteous indignation made his plea sound heartbreakingly noble.

Sure enough, Nie Mingjue’s blade locked midair. Veins bulged along his temples, frozen in conflicted torment. He tightened his white-knuckled grip on the hilt, roaring: "Fine! Once I hack you to pieces, I’ll take my own life to pay the blood debt!"

Having blown his top, Meng Yao instantly shrank back in terror. Seeing Baxia crashing down to cleave him in two, his soul nearly left his body; spinning on his heel, he sprinted for dear life. One swung and the other scrambled, both battered, blood-drenched, and stumbling over their own feet. Trapped in the middle of this dark comedy, Wei Wuxian was having the time of his life—hacking away at the future Chief Cultivator while laughing his ass off internally. He knew for a fact that if Nie Mingjue hadn't been crippled by his wounds, Meng Yao would have been diced into mincemeat minutes ago.

Amidst the chaotic chase, an astonished voice rang through the trees: "Mingjue-xiong!"

A pristine figure in flowing white stepped out from the foliage. Catching sight of him, Meng Yao looked as if he’d laid eyes on a divine savior, scrambling on all fours to duck behind the man’s robes: "Ze-wu-jun! Ze-wu-jun, save me!"

Blinded by incandescent rage, Nie Mingjue didn't even pause to question why Lan Xichen had appeared in Qishan. He roared, "Xichen, out of the way!"

Baxia came down with earth-shattering momentum. Left with no choice, Lan Xichen drew Shuoshuang, stepping into the path of the blow to parry the strike with a heavy metallic ring. "Mingjue-xiong, calm yourself! Why must you resort to this?!"

Nie Mingjue snarled, "Why don't you ask this rat what he did?!"

Lan Xichen glanced back at Meng Yao, who was trembling like a cornered rabbit, stammering with lowered eyes as if too terrified to speak. Nie Mingjue sneered, "Back when he fled Langya, I wondered why I couldn't dig him up even if I tore the earth apart! Turns out he crawled straight into the Wen dogs' kennel, playing the butcher's lapdog in Nightless City!"

"Mingjue-xiong," Lan Xichen said gently.

He rarely ever interrupted anyone. Nie Mingjue paused, startled, as Lan Xichen continued, "Do you know who provided the battle formations and troop deployments for the Qishan Wen Sect all those times?"

Nie Mingjue frowned. "You."

"I was merely the courier," Lan Xichen countered softly. "Do you know who the original source of that intelligence was?"

Standing in the shadow of the mountain, the implication landed like a hammer. Nie Mingjue stared at Meng Yao cowering behind Lan Xichen's robes, his brow twitching in sheer disbelief.

Lan Xichen pressed on, "There is no mistake. I received his secret missive today, which was why I came to extract him. Otherwise, how could I have happened upon this exact path?"

Nie Mingjue was struck entirely dumb.

"After the incident in Langya," Lan Xichen explained, "A-Yao was consumed by remorse, yet terrified of facing your wrath. He saw no path forward other than infiltrating the Wen Clan, earning Wen Ruohan's trust so he could secretly funnel intelligence to me. At first, even I did not know the spy's identity; it was only through a stroke of coincidence that I unraveled the cipher and realized it was him." He turned slightly, whispering to Meng Yao, "Did you not explain this to Mingjue-xiong?"

Clutching the bloody cut on his arm, Meng Yao offered a miserable, bitter smile. "Ze-wu-jun, you saw for yourself... Even if I had spoken, Sect Leader Nie would never have believed a word I said."

Nie Mingjue remained silent. Baxia and Shuoshuang stayed locked in a tense standoff, their edges shivering with residual spiritual hum. Meng Yao stared at the clashing steel with visible dread, yet after an agonizing pause, he stepped out from behind Lan Xichen’s robes and dropped heavily to his knees before Nie Mingjue.

Lan Xichen murmured, "Meng Yao?"

Lowering his head, Meng Yao choked out, "Sect Leader Nie... back in the Sun Palace, though it was done to deceive Wen Ruohan and keep him from smelling a trap, I struck you, spoke treasonous insolence, and deliberately picked at the wound of your late father... Dire as the circumstances were, I am truly, deeply sorry."

Nie Mingjue’s voice was cold as iron: "You shouldn't be kneeling to me. You should be kneeling to the allied cultivators you butchered with your own hands."

Meng Yao pleaded, "Wen Ruohan was a vicious lunatic; the slightest disobedience would trigger a bloodbath. If I were to pose as his trusted confidant, how could I stand idly by while captives insulted him to his face? So I..."

Nie Mingjue sneered, "Splendid. Sounds like this wasn't the first time you dirtied your hands."

Meng Yao let out a ragged breath. "I was in the belly of the beast."

Lan Xichen held his ground, sighing with gentle melancholy. "Mingjue-xiong... embedded deep in enemy territory, there were things... beyond his control. Taking those lives tore him apart inside as well..."

Ze-wu-jun is simply too pure-hearted for his own good, Wei Wuxian mused. Yet reflecting on it, Wei Wuxian only harbored deep suspicion because he knew the grim fate awaiting everyone down the line; in Lan Xichen’s eyes right now, Meng Yao was an undercover hero enduring unbearable humiliation and risking his neck for the righteous cause. Walking in different shoes, how could their perspectives ever align?

After an agonizing silence, Nie Mingjue raised Baxia once more!

Lan Xichen gasped, "Mingjue-xiong!"

Meng Yao squeezed his eyes shut in surrender. Lan Xichen gripped Shuoshuang tight, murmuring, "Pardon me—"

Before the clash could ignite, Baxia’s gleaming edge cleaved downward in a furious, blinding arc—slamming squarely into a colossal boulder beside the path.

The concussive crack of shattered stone made Meng Yao flinch. Glancing sideways, the massive boulder had been cleanly split in two from crown to base.

In the end, he couldn't bring himself to strike the killing blow. Sliding Baxia back into its scabbard with a crisp snap, Nie Mingjue turned on his heel and walked away without looking back.

With Wen Ruohan dead, the Qishan Wen Clan's remaining forces crumbled into scattered remnants, their defeat sealed once and for all.

And Meng Yao—the deep-cover operative who had spent years buried in the belly of the beast—rose to instant, legendary fame overnight.

Wei Wuxian had always wondered: since their relationship had soured so badly after Meng Yao abandoned Qinghe, why had Nie Mingjue ever agreed to take the sworn oath with him? Walking through these memories, the answer was obvious. Beyond Lan Xichen’s tireless efforts to play peacemaker, Nie Mingjue had ultimately honored the debt of having his life saved and acknowledged the vital intelligence Meng Yao had funneled to the allied front. In truth, many of his glorious victories had been paved with the intelligence Meng Yao passed through Lan Xichen. Nie Mingjue still recognized the youth's brilliant talent, hoping to guide him back onto the righteous path. And since Meng Yao was no longer his subordinate, swearing brotherhood gave him the formal standing to keep him in line—just as he disciplined his own brother, Nie Huaisang.

Following the victory of the Sunshot Campaign, the Lanling Jin Sect hosted an extravagant, multi-day flower banquet, inviting countless cultivators and prominent clans from across the realm to celebrate the dawn of a new era.

Koi Tower was teeming with celebratory crowds. From Nie Mingjue’s towering vantage point, the sea of cultivators parted like the tide, bowing low on either side to murmur reverent greetings to Chifeng-zun.

What staggering prestige, Wei Wuxian thought. These people look at Nie Mingjue with equal parts terror and awe. Plenty of people feared me back in the day, but precious few ever respected me.

Jin Guangyao was stationed beside the grand Sumeru plinth. Having taken the sworn oath with Nie Mingjue and Lan Xichen and finally being recognized by his father, his brow now bore the vermilion mark of honor. Draped in the white-and-gold Sparks Amidst Snow robes crowned with a black gauze cap, he looked completely transformed—radiant, poised, and impeccably refined. His sharp wit remained as agile as ever, but wrapped in effortless grace that far eclipsed his humble beginnings.

Standing beside him, Wei Wuxian’s eyes snagged on an all-too-familiar silhouette.

Xue Yang.

At this point in time, Xue Yang was remarkably young; though baby fat still clung to his boyish cheeks, he was already surprisingly tall. Dressed in matching Sparks Amidst Snow robes, he stood shoulder-to-shoulder with Jin Guangyao, looking like a pair of dashing young masters basking in the spring breeze. They seemed to be whispering about some inside joke; Jin Guangyao smiled, casually tossing a small hand gesture, while Xue Yang threw his head back in wild, boisterous laughter. He scanned the passing cultivators with lazy disdain, his eyes radiating pure, unadulterated contempt—as if the esteemed guests strolling by were nothing more than walking piles of garbage. Catching sight of Nie Mingjue, he showed none of the timid deference displayed by the others, instead flashing a brazen, toothy grin that showcased his sharp canines.

Noticing Nie Mingjue’s thunderous glare, Jin Guangyao hastily wiped the smile from his face, leaning in to whisper a quick reprimand. Xue Yang waved a flippant hand, swaggering off in the opposite direction with a careless slouch.

Jin Guangyao stepped forward, bowing respectfully. "Eldest Brother."

Nie Mingjue snapped, "Who was that?"

After a beat of hesitation, Jin Guangyao replied cautiously, "Xue Yang."

Nie Mingjue’s brow furrowed into a deep scowl. "Xue Yang of Kuizhou?"

Jin Guangyao nodded. Xue Yang’s monstrous reputation had been notorious since his youth; Wei Wuxian could feel Nie Mingjue’s simmering disgust ratcheting up by the second. "Why are you associating with scum like that?"

Jin Guangyao murmured, "The Lanling Jin Clan recruited him as a guest disciple."

Not daring to dig his heels in, he made a polite excuse about greeting incoming guests and hurriedly scurried away.

Nie Mingjue shook his head in disgust, turning around.

The moment his gaze shifted, Wei Wuxian’s breath hitched in his throat—as if moonlight had suddenly cascaded from the heavens to illuminate the golden terrace.

Lan Xichen and Lan Wangji were ascending the steps side by side.

Standing together, the Twin Jades of Lan were a breathtaking spectacle: one carrying a jade xiao, the other bearing a guqin; one warm and elegant, the other aloof and crystalline. Shared ethereal beauty, yet distinct in their divine grace—a single, peerless mold cast in twin masterworks. No wonder every eye in the courtyard was glued to their approach, collective gasps of awe rippling through the crowd.

At this age, Lan Wangji’s jawline still carried a trace of youthful softness, yet his expression was already locked behind that familiar, frosty wall that kept the mortal world at arm's length. Wei Wuxian’s gaze locked onto that porcelain face, utterly incapable of tearing his eyes away. Whether the man could hear him or not, he belted out with unrestrained, giddy joy:

Lan Zhan! I missed you to death! Hahahahahahaha!

Suddenly, a clear, crisp voice broke the reverie: "Sect Leader Nie. Sect Leader Lan."

Hearing that familiar cadence, Wei Wuxian’s heart did a violent jolt. Nie Mingjue turned toward the greeting.

Draped in deep violet robes, Jiang Cheng strode forward with a hand resting on his sword hilt.

And standing right beside him was Wei Wuxian himself.

He saw his past self: draped in sweeping black robes, hands tucked casually behind his back, a pitch-black bamboo flute with a vibrant crimson tassel tucked into his sash. He carried no sword. Flanking Jiang Cheng, he offered a lazy, polite nod toward the gathered sect leaders—his posture carrying an unmistakable, arrogant swagger, looking down on the world like an untouchable, enigmatic sovereign.

Watching his teenage self putting on such grand, haughty airs, a wave of profound secondhand embarrassment washed over Wei Wuxian. His teeth ached from pure cringe, burning with a sudden, violent urge to sprint over and beat the smug little bastard to a bloody pulp.

Lan Wangji’s eyes drifted toward the black-robed youth beside Jiang Cheng, his brow giving a microscopic twitch before his pale gaze slid smoothly away, staring straight ahead with immaculate, unshakeable composure. Jiang Cheng and Nie Mingjue exchanged stiff, solemn nods—neither being men of many words—and after brief pleasantries, the two groups parted ways.

Wei Wuxian watched as his past self glanced left and right, his dark eyes catching Lan Wangji’s silhouette across the terrace. He was just about to open his mouth to call out when Jiang Cheng stepped up beside him. Both youths dipped their heads, exchanging a quick, deadpan exchange; the black-robed Wei Wuxian burst into bright, boisterous laughter, throwing his arm over Jiang Cheng's shoulder as they sauntered off toward the banquet hall.

All around them, the sea of visiting cultivators parted like the tide, hurriedly clearing a wide, empty berth around their path.

Wei Wuxian racked his brain trying to remember what on earth they had been talking about back then. At first, he drew a total blank, but tracking the angle of Nie Mingjue’s gaze, he read their lips across the terrace and the memory snapped into focus.

Back then, he had leaned in and snickered, "Hey Jiang Cheng, Chifeng-zun is way taller than you. Look at that, haha."

To which Jiang Cheng had immediately fired back, "Fuck off. You're cruising for a beating."

Nie Mingjue’s eyes drifted back toward them, brow furrowing. "Why isn't Wei Ying wearing a sword?"

Carrying one's spiritual blade was a basic tenet of clan etiquette. Lan Wangji murmured evenly, "He likely forgot."

Nie Mingjue arched an eyebrow. "How do you 'forget' your own sword?"

Lan Wangji’s tone stayed flat. "It is hardly unheard of for him."

Wei Wuxian scoffed inwardly: Oh, real nice. Talking shit behind my back—and I caught you red-handed.

Lan Xichen chuckled softly beside them. "Young Master Wei once mentioned that he has no patience for ceremonial red tape. He claimed that whether he wears a sword or struts around stark naked, nobody could do a damn thing to stop him anyway. Ah, youth."

Hearing his own arrogant teenage bravado parroted back to him through Lan Xichen’s lips was excruciating. A hot wave of secondhand embarrassment washed over Wei Wuxian, leaving him thoroughly mortified. Just then, Lan Wangji’s voice dropped into a low, barely audible murmur:

"Reckless."

The word was so quiet it felt meant entirely for Lan Wangji's own ears. Yet it struck Wei Wuxian’s borrowed senses like a bell, making his pulse skip two erratic beats for reasons he couldn't quite name.

Lan Xichen cast an amused glance sideways. "Oh? Why are you still standing here?"

Lan Wangji blinked, his deadpan expression shifting into subtle bewilderment. "Brother is here, so naturally I remain here."

Lan Xichen nudged him gently. "Why haven't you gone over to speak with him? They're about to walk out of range."

Wei Wuxian was genuinely flabbergasted. What’s Ze-wu-jun playing at? Did Lan Zhan actually have something he wanted to say to me back then?

Before he could see how Lan Wangji would react, a violent commotion erupted from the other side of the Sumeru terrace. His own furious roar echoed across the stone:

"Jin Zixuan! Don't you dare forget what you said and did in the past! What the hell is this supposed to mean now?!"

The memory hit Wei Wuxian like a bucket of cold water. Ah. It was that day!

Across the courtyard, Jin Zixuan’s voice fired right back, brimming with aristocratic fury: "I was addressing Sect Leader Jiang, not you! My inquiries concerned Lady Jiang—what business is it of yours?!"

"Brilliant point!" Wei Wuxian barked. "What business does my shijie have with you?! Who was the arrogant bastard whose eyes were lodged so high up his forehead he couldn't even see straight back then?!"

Jin Zixuan wheeled on Jiang Cheng. "Sect Leader Jiang! This is my clan's banquet, and this is a member of your house! Are you going to rein him in or not?!"

Lan Xichen sighed. "Why must they bicker at every turn?"

Lan Wangji’s gaze locked onto the fray, though his boots remained rooted to the pavers. After an agonizing beat of hesitation, as if finally making up his mind, he took a decisive stride forward—only for Jiang Cheng’s sharp snap to ring out:

"Shut your mouth, Wei Wuxian! Young Master Jin, my apologies. My sister is doing very well; thank you for your concern. We can revisit this discussion another time."

Wei Wuxian scoffed coldly, "Another time? There is no 'another time'! Whether she’s well or not is none of his damn business! Who does he think he is?!"

With a sharp flick of his sleeve, he turned on his heel and stormed off. Jiang Cheng barked after him, "Get back here! Where do you think you're going?!"

Wei Wuxian waved a flippant hand over his shoulder. "Anywhere! Anywhere that keeps me from looking at that peacock's face! I never wanted to come to this farce in the first place—handle it yourself!"

Jiang Cheng’s face darkened with storm clouds as Wei Wuxian left him in the dust. Jin Guangyao, who had been darting around the banquet floor smoothing out awkward corners and greeting guests with flawless charm, immediately hurried over at the first whiff of trouble. "Young Master Wei, please, stay your steps!"

Hands tucked behind his back, Wei Wuxian walked at a blistering clip, his expression thunderous, oblivious to the eyes tracking him. Lan Wangji stepped into his path, but before a single word could pass his lips, the two of them brushed shoulders and Wei Wuxian breezed right past him without looking back.

Unable to catch up, Jin Guangyao stamped his foot in helpless dismay. "Ah, he's gone... Sect Leader Jiang, what... what should we do?"

Smoothing the fury from his brow, Jiang Cheng said coldly, "Pay him no mind. He runs wild at home and has no sense of decorum." With that, he turned back to smooth things over with Jin Zixuan.

Watching the two of them, Wei Wuxian let out a long, silent sigh. Fortunately, Nie Mingjue had zero interest in teenage drama and looked away, pulling Wei Wuxian’s vision elsewhere.

The scene shifted to the Unclean Realm, the seat of the Qinghe Nie Sect.

Nie Mingjue sat cross-legged on a straw mat, facing Lan Xichen, who had a seven-stringed zither resting before him. Plucking the final chord, the crystalline music faded into the hall. Jin Guangyao laughed softly. "Well, having heard Second Brother play, I might as well smash my own zither the moment I get home."

Lan Xichen smiled gently. "Third Brother's zither skills are among the finest outside of Gusu. Did your mother teach you?"

Jin Guangyao shook his head. "No. I picked it up on my own by watching others. She never taught me arts like this; she only drilled me in reading and writing, spending exorbitant sums to buy me sword manuals and cultivation scriptures."

Lan Xichen looked surprised. "Cultivation manuals?"

Jin Guangyao chuckled self-deprecatingly. "Second Brother, you must never have seen them. The cheap little pamphlets sold in roadside markets—scribbled with chaotic sketches of figures and stuffed with pretentious, cryptic nonsense." Lan Xichen shook his head with an amused smile, and Jin Guangyao mirrored the gesture. "Total swindles, designed purely to fleece naive women like my mother and ignorant children. Practicing them won't kill you, but they won't grant you a speck of true spiritual power either."

He let out a wistful sigh. "Yet how could my mother know any better? The moment she saw them, she bought them no matter the price, always saying that when the day came for me to meet my father, I had to present myself accomplished and capable, never falling behind his legitimate heirs. Every copper we had went into those books."

Lan Xichen plucked a few strings, murmuring, "To achieve such proficiency through mere observation proves your innate talent. Under the tutelage of a renowned master, your progress would be boundless."

Jin Guangyao beamed. "A renowned master sits right before my eyes, though I wouldn't dare presume."

"Why shouldn't you? Please, take a seat."

Jin Guangyao eagerly settled across from him, straightening his posture like a dedicated pupil. "What will Teacher Lan instruct today?"

"How about the Song of Clarity?"

Jin Guangyao’s eyes lit up. Before he could speak, Nie Mingjue looked up from his scrolls. "Second Brother, the Song of Clarity is one of your clan's sacred arts. Do not let it leak to outsiders."

Lan Xichen waved the concern off with an easy smile. "The Song of Clarity is distinct from the Song of Disruption; its sole purpose is to cleanse the heart and anchor the mind. Why should one hoard a craft meant for healing? Besides, imparting it to Third Brother... how could that ever be considered leaking to an outsider?"

Seeing that Lan Xichen had made up his mind, Nie Mingjue dropped the matter.

Sometime later, Nie Mingjue returned to the Unclean Realm. The moment he stepped into the main hall, his eyes caught Nie Huaisang hunched over a long table, meticulously admiring a row of over a dozen unfolded, gold-painted folding fans. He stroked each one with reverent obsession, muttering under his breath as he compared the poetic inscriptions brushstroke by brushstroke.

Veins bulged along Nie Mingjue’s temples. "Nie Huaisang!"

Nie Huaisang hit the floor instantly.

He dropped straight to his knees out of sheer, unadulterated panic, trembling violently as he scrambled upright. "B-b-b-brother!"

Nie Mingjue barked, "Where is your saber?!"

Nie Huaisang stammered, sweating bullets, "In... in my room. No, wait, on the training grounds! No, hold on, let me... let me think..."

Wei Wuxian could feel Nie Mingjue’s urge to cleave the boy in half right then and there: "You haul around a dozen decorative fans wherever you go, yet you don't even know where your own spiritual weapon is?!"

Nie Huaisang squeaked, "I'll go find it right now!"

"Don't bother! Finding it won't magically make you practice anyway. Burn the lot of them!"

Nie Huaisang paled in horror, frantically scooping the delicate fans into his chest like a mother hen shielding her chicks. "No, Brother, please! These were gifts from friends!"

Nie Mingjue slammed a palm down, splintering the wooden table clean through. "Who gave them to you?! Tell them to crawl their ass in here right now!"

A calm voice called from the entrance: "I gave them to him."

Jin Guangyao strolled into the hall. Catching sight of him, Nie Huaisang looked as though he’d laid eyes on a divine savior, practically weeping with joy: "Third Brother! You're here!"

In truth, it wasn't that Jin Guangyao possessed some magical aura that soothed Nie Mingjue’s volcanic temper; rather, whenever Jin Guangyao arrived, Nie Mingjue’s fury inevitably redirected entirely onto him, leaving no breath left to scold anyone else. In that sense, calling him Nie Huaisang’s savior was hardly an exaggeration. Overjoyed, Nie Huaisang showered him with enthusiastic greetings while desperately shoving the armful of fans into his tunic.

Watching his little brother's pathetic scramble, Nie Mingjue’s fury peaked so hard it circled right back into bitter amusement. He wheeled on Jin Guangyao: "Stop gifting him these frivolous, useless trinkets!"

Flustered, Nie Huaisang fumbled, dropping two fans to the floorboards. Jin Guangyao scooped them up, brushing off the dust before tucking them gently back into the boy's arms. "Huaisang appreciates elegance and has a passion for poetry and painting. He indulges in no vice or wicked habits—how can you call that 'frivolous'?"

Nie Huaisang nodded frantically. "Exactly! Third Brother is completely right!"

Nie Mingjue sneered, "A sect leader has no use for poetry and painting."

Nie Huaisang mumbled, "It's not like I'm ever going to be sect leader anyway! You can just do it forever, Brother, I don't want the job!"

A murderous glare from his older brother clamped his jaw shut instantly.

Nie Mingjue turned back to Jin Guangyao. "What are you doing here?"

Jin Guangyao smiled warmly. "Second Brother mentioned he gifted you a guqin."

The instrument had been brought over by Lan Xichen to play the Song of Clarity, helping to soothe Nie Mingjue’s volatile spiritual hum. Jin Guangyao continued, "Lately, the Gusu Lan Clan's reconstruction of Cloud Recesses has reached a critical juncture. You forbade him from making the journey, so Second Brother taught the Song of Clarity to me instead. Though my playing cannot hold a candle to Second Brother's mastery, I hoped it might offer you a fraction of relief and balance your meridians."

Nie Mingjue replied bluntly, "Tend to your own affairs and that will be plenty."

Nie Huaisang perked up with immense curiosity. "Third Brother, what song is it? Can I listen? Oh, by the way, that out-of-print manuscript you hunted down for me last time..."

Nie Mingjue roared, "Get the hell back to your room!"

Nie Huaisang tucked his tail between his legs and bolted, though he was definitely heading toward the guest parlor to raid whatever other presents Jin Guangyao had brought along. With the interruptions, Nie Mingjue’s anger had mostly burned out. Looking at Jin Guangyao, he noted the faint weariness in his face, his gold-trimmed robes dusted with the grime of the road—he had clearly ridden straight from Carp Tower without resting.

Nie Mingjue paused, softening his tone. "Sit."

Jin Guangyao inclined his head and took a seat. "Eldest Brother, since you care so deeply for Huaisang, a gentler approach would yield far better results. Why must you always resort to fire and brimstone?"

Nie Mingjue grunted, "I could hold a blade to his throat and he still wouldn't budge. The boy is utterly hopeless."

"Huaisang isn't hopeless," Jin Guangyao argued gently. "His passions simply lie elsewhere."

Nie Mingjue arched an eyebrow. "You certainly seem to have his passions mapped out down to the inch."

Jin Guangyao chuckled. "Naturally. Is that not my greatest talent? The only heart I can never seem to read... is yours, Eldest Brother."

Understanding a person's vices and desires was the easiest way to manipulate them, yielding twice the result with half the effort; Jin Guangyao was an undisputed master of psychological dissection. Only with Nie Mingjue did he hit a brick wall. Wei Wuxian had seen it firsthand back when Meng Yao served as his adjutant: the man touched neither wine nor women, cared nothing for wealth, viewed antiques and poetry as glorified mud and ink, and drank exquisite vintage tea with the exact same indifference as street-stall dregs. Meng Yao had racked his brain trying to sniff out a single weakness, only to realize Chifeng-zun cared for nothing beyond honing his saber and butchering Wen dogs—an impenetrable, walking iron fortress.

Hearing that self-deprecating jest, Nie Mingjue’s irritation smoothed over. "Stop enabling his lazy habits."

Jin Guangyao smiled softly. "Where is Second Brother's guqin, Eldest Brother?"

Nie Mingjue gestured toward the side table.

From that day forward, Jin Guangyao rode from Lanling to Qinghe every few days without fail, diligently playing the Song of Clarity to ground Nie Mingjue’s spiritual core—tireless and utterly without complaint. The melody was undeniably miraculous; Wei Wuxian could feel the simmering hostility in Nie Mingjue’s chest slowly receding beneath the notes. During those musical sessions, the conversations between the two settled into a tranquil harmony they hadn't shared since the war. Wei Wuxian began to suspect that Lan Xichen's supposed busywork in Gusu had been an intentional excuse all along—a delicate white lie designed to give the two estranged brothers a chance to mend their fractured bond.

Yet the moment that thought crossed his mind, a violent, volcanic fury detonated in his chest.

Nie Mingjue shoved past two trembling guards who didn't dare raise a hand to stop him, storming straight into the Fragrance Pavilion. Inside the study, Lan Xichen and Jin Guangyao were leaning over a desk, deep in solemn discussion over an array of annotated blueprints.

Seeing him kick the door open, Lan Xichen blinked in surprise. "Eldest Brother?"

Nie Mingjue barked, "Stay where you are." Turning an icy glare onto Jin Guangyao, he growled, "You. Outside."

Jin Guangyao exchanged a quick, meaningful glance with Lan Xichen before smiling placidly. "Second Brother, could you help me review this clause? I need to attend to some private business with Eldest Brother; I'll return shortly for your guidance."

A ripple of worry crossed Lan Xichen’s brow, but Jin Guangyao offered a reassuring nod, stepping out into the garden behind Nie Mingjue. The moment they reached the balustrade overlooking the courtyard, Nie Mingjue unleashed a concussive palm strike!

The surrounding disciples cried out in horror. Jin Guangyao twisted his frame with supple agility, effortlessly dodging the blow. Raising a hand to signal the guards to stand down, he smiled calmly at Nie Mingjue. "Eldest Brother, why must we resort to blows? Let us speak reasonably."

Nie Mingjue snapped, "Where is Xue Yang?"

Jin Guangyao replied smoothly, "He has been thrown into the deepest dungeon, sentenced to life imprisonment without release—"

"What did you promise me to my face?!"

Jin Guangyao fell silent.

Nie Mingjue’s voice was like grinding steel: "I demanded blood for blood, and you give him life imprisonment?!"

Jin Guangyao pleaded cautiously, "So long as he is punished and stripped of any chance to commit harm, is a life sentence not functionally the same as an execution...?"

"You recommended that butcher to your clan! You vouched for his character! And even now, you dare cover for his crimes?!"

"I am not covering for him!" Jin Guangyao protested. "The tragedy of the Yueyang Chang Clan shocked me to my core! How could I have anticipated that Xue Yang would slaughter over fifty innocent souls in cold blood?! But my father insists on keeping him alive..."

Nie Mingjue scoffed with venomous mockery, "Shocked?! Who recruited him? Who promoted him? Who put power in his hands?! Stop hiding behind your father's skirts—do you honestly expect me to believe you had no clue what Xue Yang was up to?!"

Jin Guangyao sighed, sounding thoroughly exhausted. "Eldest Brother, it truly was my father's command. I have no power to defy him. If you force me to execute Xue Yang now, how am I supposed to answer to him?"

Nie Mingjue’s patience shattered. "Spare me your drivel. Bring me Xue Yang’s head, or don't bother showing your face."

Jin Guangyao opened his mouth to argue, but Nie Mingjue cut him off with a thunderous roar: "Meng Yao! Stop singing your sweet tunes in front of me—your cheap parlor tricks stopped working on me years ago!"

A flicker of raw, humiliated agony flashed across Jin Guangyao’s face—like a man with a shameful, rotting illness stripped bare under the noon sun, exposed and cornered with nowhere to hide.

His voice dropped, trembling faintly: "My tricks? What tricks? Eldest Brother, you constantly sneer at me for being calculating and underhanded. You claim you walk upright, fearless of heaven and earth, a righteous hero who has no need for schemes and shadows. Fine! You were born into nobility with monstrous cultivation! But what about me?! Am I like you?! I had no immense core or solid foundation—who the hell ever taught me anything growing up?! I had no prestigious clan backing me. Do you honestly think my footing in the Lanling Jin Sect is secure?! You think Jin Zixuan’s death magically cleared the path for me to soar to the heavens?! Jin Guangshan would rather drag another stray bastard home from the gutter than consider naming me his heir! You want me to fear nothing under heaven and earth?! I am terrified of heaven, I am terrified of the earth, and I am terrified of people! It's easy to stand on high moral ground when you’ve never starved a day in your life!"

Nie Mingjue stared at him with chilling contempt. "Strip away the excuses, and all you are saying is that you refuse to execute Xue Yang because you cannot bear to let your petty status in the Jin Clan waver."

"Of course I can't!" Jin Guangyao hissed.

Lifting his head, an eerie, feral fire danced behind his dark eyes. "Though, Eldest Brother, there is a question I have burned to ask you for years: the blood on your hands far eclipses mine! Why is it that when I was forced by desperate circumstances to execute a handful of allied cultivators, you hold it over my head to this very day?!"

Nie Mingjue let out a harsh, furious laugh. "Fine! I’ll answer you! Countless souls have fallen to my saber, but never once have I taken a life for personal desire—and I have never, ever murdered to climb the ladder of power!"

Jin Guangyao smiled bitterly. "I see. So what you mean to say, Eldest Brother, is that every single person you butchered had it coming?"

Drawing upon some manic well of defiance, he chuckled twice, closing the distance between them as his voice rose in sharp, mocking challenge: "Then tell me: who appointed you judge to determine whether a soul deserves to die?! Is your moral compass the absolute law of the universe?! If I slaughter one person to save a hundred, is that a crime deserving death, or an act of greater good?! Great achievements demand sacrifice!"

Nie Mingjue’s voice dropped like an executioner's blade: "Then why didn't you sacrifice yourself?! Are you somehow nobler than them?! Are you fundamentally different from the people you butchered?!"

Jin Guangyao stared into his eyes. After an agonizing, frozen silence—as if casting aside his final shackle—he spoke with icy, absolute calm:

"Yes."

Lifting his chin, his expression warped into a terrifying cocktail of arrogance, cold clarity, and quiet madness:

"I am, without question, completely different from them!"

That insolence was the final spark on the powder keg.

Nie Mingjue’s boot lashed out. Caught entirely without spiritual defense, Jin Guangyao didn't even attempt to dodge; the kick landed squarely against his sternum, sending him tumbling violently down the grand staircase of Koi Tower.

Nie Mingjue looked down from the landing, his roar echoing across the terrace:

"The son of a whore—no wonder you turned out like this!"

Jin Guangyao tumbled down more than fifty stone steps before crashing onto the lower plaza. He didn't linger on the stone for even a second, scrambling straight back to his feet. Raising a hand, he waved off the alarmed disciples rushing toward him, brushed the dust from his golden robes, and slowly lifted his head to meet Nie Mingjue’s gaze. His eyes were chillingly serene—bordering on total apathy.

Nie Mingjue’s saber cleared its sheath with a menacing rasp. Hearing the commotion, Lan Xichen hurried out from the pavilion; taking in the scene, his own blade, Shuoshuang, cleared its scabbard in an instant. "What is the meaning of this?!"

Jin Guangyao bowed with eerie politeness. "Nothing at all. I thank Eldest Brother for his instruction."

Nie Mingjue barked, "Xichen, stay out of this!"

"Sheathe your blade, Eldest Brother!" Lan Xichen urged, alarmed. "Your mind is clouded!"

"My mind is clear! I know exactly what I am doing! He is beyond redemption—leave him unchecked and he will plunge the world into ruin! Killing him now saves the realm from disaster!"

Lan Xichen froze, horrified. "How can you say such a thing?! He has ridden between Qinghe and Lanling for weeks without rest, pouring his soul into soothing your meridians—is 'beyond redemption' all that effort earns him?!"

With a man of Nie Mingjue’s rigid honor, throwing debts and grievances into his face was the most effective counter; his saber arm stiffened, his gaze drifting toward Jin Guangyao. Blood was pouring freely down the man's temple. Beyond the fresh bruises from the fall, an old, bandaged wound peeked out—previously concealed beneath his black gauze cap, now knocked askew. With old and new gashes tearing open at once, Jin Guangyao calmly peeled the soaked linen away, dabbing at the crimson flow so as not to ruin his fine silk robes, and tossed the cloth into the dirt. He stood there in chilling silence, staring into the distance.

Lan Xichen turned back. "Third Brother, go inside. I will speak with Eldest Brother."

Jin Guangyao offered a deep, formal bow and turned to leave without a word. Feeling the killing intent dissipate from Nie Mingjue’s frame, Lan Xichen sheathed his sword, guiding him gently by the shoulder toward the gardens.

"Eldest Brother," Lan Xichen murmured softly, "you may not realize it, but A-Yao’s position right now is dreadfully precarious."

Nie Mingjue’s tone remained frigid. "To hear him tell it, he is perpetually drowning in misery."

Yet his saber clicked smoothly back into its scabbard.

Lan Xichen sighed. "Is he entirely wrong? Did you not notice his outburst just now? Would he have ever spoken to you like that in the past?"

It was true. It was wholly uncharacteristic. Jin Guangyao was never one to lose his cool; he knew better than anyone that surviving Nie Mingjue required absolute deference. That raw, desperate explosion of venom was unprecedented.

Lan Xichen continued, "Madame Jin has never favored him, and since Zixuan-xiong’s passing, she takes her grief out on him with daily verbal lashes and beatings. His father ignores his counsel entirely, tossing aside every reform he submits."

Wei Wuxian recalled the architectural blueprints on the desk earlier, realizing instantly: The Watchtowers.

Finally, Lan Xichen pleaded, "Do not corner him so harshly. I believe he understands what must be done. We simply need to grant him a little more time."

Nie Mingjue grunted, "Let us hope so."

Wei Wuxian assumed that taking a boot down the stairs would keep Jin Guangyao away for a while. Yet a few days later, the man arrived at the Unclean Realm right on schedule.

Nie Mingjue was out on the training grounds personally drilling Nie Huaisang in saber forms, ignoring his sworn brother entirely. Jin Guangyao waited at the edge of the courtyard with immaculate manners, offering no complaint. Uninterested in martial arts and baking under the scorching sun, Nie Huaisang’s swings were comically half-assed; after barely three strikes, he whined about exhaustion, skipping over toward Jin Guangyao to see what presents had been brought along.

Usually, Nie Mingjue would merely scowl. Today, his temper detonated: "Nie Huaisang! Are you begging for my blade across your skull?! Get your ass back here!"

Had Nie Huaisang possessed Wei Wuxian's spiritual empathy to feel the volcanic pressure bubbling in his brother's chest, he never would have dared giggle. Instead, he whined, "Brother, the hour is up! Time for a break!"

Nie Mingjue snapped, "You took a break an incense stick ago! Back to your forms, until you master them!"

Nie Huaisang waved it off carelessly. "I'm never going to learn it anyway! I'm done for today!"

It was a line he tossed out regularly, but Nie Mingjue’s reaction was terrifyingly explosive. He roared, "I could drill a pig into mastering this form—how the hell can I not teach you?!"

Stunned by the sudden fury, Nie Huaisang shrank back like a terrified rabbit, diving behind Jin Guangyao’s robes. Seeing the two of them huddled together poured oil on the fire: "A year on a single form, and you cry exhaustion after standing in the sun for five minutes! I don't ask you to be a legend, but you can barely protect your own skin! How did the Qinghe Nie Clan produce a piece of garbage like you?! Both of you should be tied to a post and flogged daily! Clear out his quarters—bring everything out here!"

The order was barked at the surrounding disciples. Seeing them run off, Nie Huaisang panicked. Moments later, a line of disciples returned carrying armfuls of calligraphy scrolls, fine porcelain, and decorative fans from his chambers. Nie Mingjue had threatened to torch his treasures countless times, but had never followed through; realizing this was no drill, Nie Huaisang shrieked, lunging forward: "Brother! No! You can't burn them!"

Sensing disaster, Jin Guangyao chimed in, "Eldest Brother, please, do not be rash—"

Nie Mingjue’s saber lashed out with a concussive burst of spiritual fire, instantly engulfing the delicate treasures in a roaring wall of flames! Nie Huaisang wailed, throwing himself toward the blaze, but Jin Guangyao grabbed his collar, dragging him back: "Huaisang, careful!"

Nie Mingjue unleashed an empty-handed palm strike; the two porcelain vases Nie Huaisang had managed to snatch from the embers shattered into dust in his grip, while his precious scrolls and paintings were reduced to floating cinders within seconds. Nie Huaisang stood paralyzed, watching the cherished collection he had spent a lifetime gathering burn to ash.

Jin Guangyao checked the boy's blistered hands with genuine concern. "Did you burn yourself?" Turning to the disciples, he urged, "Quickly, fetch soothing salves!"

The attendants scurried off. Nie Huaisang stood rooted to the dirt, trembling violently from head to toe as his eyes went bloodshot, staring fixedly at Nie Mingjue. Sensing the dangerous shift in the boy's breathing, Jin Guangyao draped an arm over his shoulders, murmuring, "Huaisang, are you alright? Don't look at it anymore. Let us go inside to rest."

Nie Huaisang’s eyes were crimson, his jaw locked tight. Jin Guangyao coaxed softly, "Things can be replaced; Third Brother will hunt down more for you later..."

Nie Mingjue’s voice was pure winter frost: "Bring them through my gates again, and I will burn them again."

A sudden, terrifying flash of pure hatred tore across Nie Huaisang’s face. He hurled his spiritual saber violently against the stone floor, screaming at the top of his lungs:

"Go ahead and burn them, then!!!"

Jin Guangyao blanched. "Huaisang! Your brother is furious, do not—"

Nie Huaisang rounded on Nie Mingjue, howling with raw, unhinged fury:

"Saber, saber, saber! Who the fuck wants to practice this piece of shit art anyway?! What if I'm happy being a useless piece of garbage, huh?! Whoever wants to be sect leader can take the damn job! I don't know how to do it and I don't like it! What is the point of forcing me?!"
